bug_semantics: The standalone telemetry and key servers silently substituted PostgreSQL connection strings containing predictable username/password pairs when DATABASE_URL was absent: telemetry:telemetry in server/telemetry-server/app/config.py and keyserver:keyserver in server/key-server/app/config.py. server/telemetry-server/app/database.py passed settings.database_url directly to SQLAlchemy create_engine(). Consequently, an operator could start a server against a PostgreSQL deployment using shipped credentials rather than being forced to provision a secret; an unauthenticated attacker who could reach that PostgreSQL service could authenticate directly with the well-known pair and read or modify its data.
flaw_origin: The vulnerability first existed at 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35, which created the telemetry standalone server and wrote the exact fallback postgresql://telemetry:telemetry@localhost:5432/telemetry in server/telemetry-server/app/config.py. Its direct parent did not contain that path. The child commit fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4 later duplicated the same flawed design in the new key-server config with postgresql://keyserver:keyserver@localhost/keyserver; that expands the affected surface but is not the case-onset BIC.
ai_marker: BIC commit object 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35 has human author and committer Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>, and contains the exact message marker "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)" plus the exact trailer "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". The AI decision uses only this BIC commit object.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-v4vm-4xf2-fhqj (API: https://api.github.com/repos/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security-advisories/GHSA-v4vm-4xf2-fhqj) quotes server/key-server/app/config.py:33-34 and server/telemetry-server/app/config.py:29-31, explains the keyserver:keyserver and telemetry:telemetry defaults and same-network PostgreSQL attack, declares pip range < 1.4.0, and names resolution commit 57e618d. Public alias record: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c472-7fxr-552c. `git log --all --reverse -S'postgresql://telemetry:telemetry@localhost:5432/telemetry' -- server/telemetry-server/app/config.py` and `git log -L 28,31:server/telemetry-server/app/config.py 57e618d32eab5163a329a69389f1f75f81fdc90b^` show that 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35 added the four-line database fallback from /dev/null and that 57e618d32eab5163a329a69389f1f75f81fdc90b removed it. `git show -s --format=raw 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35` gives direct parent 457f88d09cc365cdbb85b083a29f0956804730be; `git cat-file -e 457f88d09cc365cdbb85b083a29f0956804730be:server/telemetry-server/app/config.py` fails because the entire path is absent, proving parent-tree absence. The BIC is a one-parent monolithic feature commit, not a merge; all-ref exact-string history exposes no finer member commit to decompose. Per-path provenance for the second advisory line is `git log -L 32,35:server/key-server/app/config.py 57e618d32eab5163a329a69389f1f75f81fdc90b^`, which shows later child fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4 created the keyserver fallback from /dev/null. Fix commit and patch: https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/57e618d32eab5163a329a69389f1f75f81fdc90b; it replaces both standalone fallback URLs with os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "") and adds startup validation that raises outside debug mode when DATABASE_URL is missing. `git tag --contains` for 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35, fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4, and 57e618d32eab5163a329a69389f1f75f81fdc90b begins at v1.4.0; no v1.3.x tag contains them, `git cat-file -e v1.3.6:server/telemetry-server/app/config.py` confirms that the last 1.3.x tag lacks the path, and the v1.4.0 tree contains the empty DATABASE_URL fallback. Thus repository tags show vulnerable development history repaired before the first containing release, v1.4.0; the advisory's literal < 1.4.0 range is not evidenced as a vulnerable tagged release, although v1.4.0 is confirmed as the fixed boundary.
reasoning: The first-party advisory identifies the exact credential-bearing configuration lines and direct fix. Exact-string -S history and line-level -L history establish independent per-path origins: telemetry at 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35 and keyserver at its child fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4. Because the telemetry fallback already made the same credential-exposure mechanism possible, 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35 is the earliest and smallest reachable case-onset BIC; the missing file in its immediate parent proves the vulnerable lines were absent. No public finer-grained member exists to decompose from the single-parent feature commit. The direct fix 57e618d32eab5163a329a69389f1f75f81fdc90b removes both hardcoded fallbacks and makes explicit database configuration mandatory in non-debug startup. Tag ancestry places BIC and fix in v1.4.0 and later, while v1.3.6 lacks the affected path, so the source history supports a vulnerable pre-release interval and a fixed v1.4.0, not exposure in an earlier tagged package. Finally, the BIC itself carries both a Claude Code generation marker and a Claude Sonnet 4.5 Co-Authored-By trailer, directly attributing AI participation to the commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism; later duplicate and fix metadata play no role in that attribution.
